## Unknown `6d` Protocol 04 Payload Groups

This isolates top-level protocol 04 `6d` server payloads as an unknown list-bearing structure. The third word is a packet-coordinate offset to a list descriptor: flag byte, little-endian entry count, then six-byte records with a prefix byte, an id at record offset +1, and a three-byte tail.

The first post-quaternion byte is followed by three little-endian doubles that land near matching static table coordinates; field semantics are still not claimed.

### Protocol 03 Variable Selector Tail Families

This groups unresolved non-`80` variable selector payloads and scans their bytes for local two-byte RPC header windows. Header windows inside these tails are boundary clues for nested or adjacent packet families; they are not decoded RPC blocks by themselves.

Across 119389 non-`80` variable selector tails, 89557 are still classified as unknown selector payloads, 20915 contain at least one known header window, and 273 contain an embedded vendor header window.

### Protocol 03 Selector 28 Effect/Emote Leads

This parses the stable prefix observed in selector `28` payloads wherever they appear in a protocol 03 object-view message: two leading bytes, a four-byte field, and a 12-byte little-endian float position when enough bytes are present. Longer payload tails are still variable; FX matches are four-byte window leads against imported FX definitions, not proof that the whole tail is decoded.

Across 7677 selector `28` payloads (6292 first-selector records), 7345 have a decodable position prefix and 5004 contain at least one imported FX ID window.

### Protocol 03 PlayerCharacter Creation Records

This parses selector `0c` player spawn/profile variable blocks against local Object12/PlayerCharacter creation attributes. The stable prefix matches `GenerateCreationPacket`: dynamic flag, little-endian GoID, spawn counter, `cd ab`, attribute count, then creation masks and fixed-width values. The full outer selector tail remains unresolved.

Across 2790 PlayerCharacter creation records, 2723 include a decoded `CharacterName` attribute.
